title: Exponential lifting for a right fibration and a right-anodyne map
statement:
Use simplicial sets, horns and internal functor simplicial sets of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and trivial Kan fibrations of [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]. A right fibration has the right lifting property against $\Lambda_j^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$ for $m\geq1$ and $0<j\leq m$. Right anodyne maps form the closure of these horn inclusions and all isomorphisms under pushouts, transfinite compositions and retracts. Let $q:E\to S$ be a right fibration of arbitrary small simplicial sets, and let $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ be right anodyne. The map
$$\rho:\operatorname{Fun}(B,E)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(B,S)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(A,S)}\operatorname{Fun}(A,E),\qquad u\longmapsto(q\circ u,u\circ i),$$
is a trivial Kan fibration. No quasicategory assumption on $E$ or $S$ is imposed.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.5.4, right-fibration/right-anodyne assertion. Kerodon tag 0154 (not the unrelated Stacks tag); read online, not archived under literature/.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary monomorphism $k:K\hookrightarrow L$ and a lifting square for $\rho$ against $k$. Unfold the internal functor construction in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For arbitrary small simplicial sets $H,V,X$, a map $a:V\to\operatorname{Fun}(H,X)$ is equivalent to $\widetilde a:H\times V\to X$: explicitly $\widetilde a_n(h,v)=a_n(v)_n(h,\operatorname{id}_{[n]})$, and the inverse sends $v\in V_n$ to the map with $m$-simplex value $(h,\alpha:[m]\to[n])\mapsto\widetilde a_m(h,V(\alpha)v)$. Naturality under simplicial operators verifies that these rules give inverse simplicial maps. Thus the lifting data specify maps $B\times K\to E$, $A\times L\to E$ agreeing on $A\times K$, and $B\times L\to S$ whose restrictions are their composites with $q$. By the colimit universal property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], glue the first two maps on their pushout $P=(A\times L)\amalg_{A\times K}(B\times K)$. Fillers of the original square correspond exactly to maps $B\times L\to E$ extending this map $P\to E$ and lying over the prescribed map to $S$.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.5.4, adjunction of its two displayed lifting problems; the explicit simplex formulas are an agent expansion of the internal-hom definition.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-product] to the given right-anodyne $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ and the monomorphism $k:K\hookrightarrow L$. Its displayed map is exactly $P\to B\times L$ in Step 1, so this map is right anodyne. This statement is about the Cartesian product, not the join used elsewhere in the ancestor route.

For the fixed $q:E\to S$, let $\mathcal L$ be the class of maps with the left lifting property against $q$, in the precise square-and-diagonal sense of [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]. Apply that node with $T$ the class consisting of $q$: $\mathcal L$ contains identities and is closed under pushouts and arrow retracts. Isomorphisms also belong to it directly, since for an isomorphism $a$ a diagonal is $u\circ a^{-1}$. By [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting] with the same singleton $T$, $\mathcal L$ is closed under all small transfinite compositions. Each generating horn $\Lambda_j^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$, $m\geq1$, $0<j\leq m$, belongs to $\mathcal L$ by the right-fibration hypothesis on $q$. The defining minimality of the weakly saturated right-anodyne class therefore puts every right-anodyne map in $\mathcal L$. In particular, the map $P\to B\times L$ of Step 2 has a lift against $q$; transposing its diagonal by Step 1 solves the arbitrary lifting problem for $\rho$.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.5.4, last sentence; explicit weak-saturation argument, compare Kerodon Corollary 4.2.4.9(2) (0151).

proof.text: Use Step 3 for $k:\partial\Delta[n]\hookrightarrow\Delta[n]$ for every $n\geq0$, using [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]. These are monomorphisms because each boundary is a simplicial subset. For $n\geq1$ the resulting fillers give precisely the required boundary extensions. For $n=0$ the domain is empty and a map $\Delta[0]\to Y$ is exactly a vertex of $Y$ (all its other values are forced degeneracies); consequently the lifting property says that every target vertex of $\rho$ has a source vertex. This is the surjectivity clause of that same definition. Thus $\rho$ is a trivial Kan fibration, with no use of a quasicategory hypothesis on $E$ or $S$.

source.place: Stacks Tag 08NL, label definition-trivial-kan, with the boundary definition immediately preceding it; applies the lifting conclusion to all boundary inclusions, including dimension zero.
